checks.context: Lambda functions are a common pivot point in cloud attacks. A function with broad IAM permissions (e.g. s3:* or iam:*) can be exploited via event injection to exfiltrate data or escalate privileges.
Without tracing, it's difficult to detect anomalous invocation patterns or trace the path of a security incident through your serverless architecture.

checks.message: X-Ray tracing explicitly set to PassThrough - tracing disabled
checks.context: PassThrough mode disables active tracing. Without it, anomalous invocation patterns and security incidents are harder to detect and trace across your serverless architecture.

Without code signing, any deployment package can be deployed to this function, including one modified by a supply chain attack or a compromised CI/CD pipeline. Code signing ensures only packages signed by a trusted publisher can be deployed. Critical for production functions handling sensitive data.

checks.message: No customer-managed KMS key specified for --kms-key-arn
checks.context: Without --kms-key-arn, Lambda uses an AWS-managed key to encrypt environment variables and SnapStart snapshots. If your compliance requirements mandate a customer-managed key for rotation control and audit trails, specify a CMK.

checks.message: Verify --environment variables do not contain plaintext secrets
checks.context: Lambda environment variables are visible in the console and CLI to anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration. Store secrets in AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store and retrieve them at runtime.

checks.message: Lambda permission granted to wildcard principal (*)
checks.context: Any AWS account in the world can invoke this function. This is almost never intentional. Scope the principal to a specific AWS account ID, service (e.g. apigateway.amazonaws.com), or ARN.

checks.message: Wildcard action grants all Lambda permissions to the principal
checks.context: Using --action * grants every Lambda action including lambda:DeleteFunction, lambda:UpdateFunctionCode, and lambda:GetFunction to the principal - not just invocation. Scope to the minimum required action, typically lambda:InvokeFunction.

checks.message: Permission granted for unauthenticated function URL access
checks.context: Setting --function-url-auth-type NONE allows anyone on the internet to invoke this function via its URL without any IAM authentication.

checks.message: Verify environment variables do not contain plaintext secrets
checks.context: Lambda environment variables are visible in the console and CLI to anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration. Store secrets in AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store and retrieve them at runtime.

checks.message: Verify the event source is trusted and the function handles malformed input safely
checks.context: Event source mappings can be exploited via event injection if the Lambda function doesn't validate input. Ensure the function sanitizes all incoming data, especially from SQS or Kinesis.

checks.message: Setting reserved concurrency to 0 will disable the function
checks.context: A reserved concurrency of 0 throttles all invocations, effectively disabling the function. This can be used as a denial-of-service vector if an attacker gains write access to Lambda configuration.
Deleting a Lambda function removes all versions and aliases. If the function is referenced by event source mappings, API Gateway, or other triggers, those integrations will break silently.

checks.message: Deploying new function code — ensure it has been reviewed for secrets and vulnerabilities
checks.context: Deploying code with hardcoded credentials, insecure dependencies, or injection vulnerabilities can compromise your entire serverless architecture. Use a CI/CD pipeline with security scanning before deployment.

checks.message: Deleting the function URL immediately breaks any application or webhook calling it
checks.context: Function URLs provide a direct HTTPS endpoint. Any external service, webhook, or application using this URL will get connection errors immediately. Update callers before deleting.

checks.message: Function URL created with no authentication - anyone on the internet can invoke it
checks.context: A function URL with AuthType=NONE allows unauthenticated invocations from any source. If the function processes sensitive data, modifies resources, or has broad IAM permissions, this is a critical exposure.

checks.message: CORS configured with wildcard origin - any website can call this function URL
checks.context: AllowOrigins=* allows any website to make cross-origin requests to your function URL. Restrict to specific trusted origins to prevent cross-site request abuse.

checks.message: Verify you are not changing auth type from AWS_IAM to NONE — this makes the endpoint public
checks.context: Switching auth type to NONE allows anyone on the internet to invoke the function. If the function processes sensitive data or has broad IAM permissions, this is a critical exposure.
